blockMcqs.question: Why is an IP address called a 'logical' address?
options: It is burned into network hardware at the factory
It is software-assigned and can change
It only works on local networks
It identifies physical cable ports
blockMcqs.explanation: Logical means software-assigned, in contrast to MAC addresses which are fixed in hardware.

blockMcqs.question: How many bits make up one IPv4 octet?
blockMcqs.explanation: An octet is 8 bits (2⁸ = 256 values, so each dotted segment ranges 0–255).

blockMcqs.question: In 192.168.1.10/24, which part is the host portion?
blockMcqs.explanation: A /24 mask means the first 24 bits (192.168.1) are network; the last 8 bits (10) identify the host.

blockMcqs.question: Which address class supports the most hosts per network?
options: Class C
Class B
Class D
Class A
blockMcqs.explanation: Class A has a /8 network portion, leaving 24 bits for hosts — about 16 million per network.

blockMcqs.question: Which is NOT an RFC 1918 private range?
blockMcqs.explanation: 198.51.100.0/24 is a documentation range (RFC 5737), not a private RFC 1918 range.

blockMcqs.question: What happens to traffic sent to 127.0.0.1?
options: It is broadcast to all LAN devices
It is routed to the nearest DNS server
It loops back to the same host without hitting the network
It is dropped by the default gateway
blockMcqs.explanation: 127.0.0.1 is the loopback address; the OS returns the traffic to itself, never sending it out.

blockMcqs.question: What does a subnet mask bit set to 1 indicate?
options: The corresponding IP bit is part of the host portion
The corresponding IP bit is part of the network portion
The address is a broadcast address
The address is private
blockMcqs.explanation: 1-bits in the mask mark network bits; 0-bits mark host bits. AND with the IP extracts the network address.

blockMcqs.question: Modern routers determine packet forwarding using:
options: The first octet's class (A, B, or C)
The MAC address class
The subnet mask and CIDR prefix
The TTL field only
blockMcqs.explanation: Classful routing is obsolete. Routers use the subnet mask (CIDR) to find the network portion and make forwarding decisions.
